steps.title: Welcome to Keepiq
steps.body: A short tour of the main screens. It takes under a minute, and you can close it at any point and pick it up again from the help menu.
Open All secrets from the menu.
steps.task: Click All secrets in the menu

steps.body: Open Features & roadmap from the menu.
steps.task: Click Features & roadmap in the menu

steps.body: Your activity and vault health live under Reports.
Flows automate the repetitive parts of this app. Have a look, though you do not have to build one now.

config.description: Your secrets, folders and applications at a glance
config._note: The nine dashboard widgets live in config.widgets[] + config.layout[], NOT in the page-level widgets[] array. CnPageRenderer renders a bare CnWidgetGrid whenever a typed page carries page-level widgets targeting the body slot, so this type:"dashboard" page never mounted CnDashboardPage and lost its header, max-width, padding, sidebar and grid discipline (hydra gate-69 page-type-discipline; hrmq#112 moved 47 pages for the same reason). Only config.widgets/config.layout reach the typed page component. Three shape differences follow from that move, all verified against the installed @conduction/nextcloud-vue dist rather than the schema prose: (1) banner/stat/text payloads move from props{} to content{}, because CnDashboardPage's registry branch passes the widget def's content BOTH as a `content` prop and spread flat, which is the dual shape those renderers document; (2) tile fields move to the widget def's TOP LEVEL, because isTile() is matched before the registry branch and CnDashboardPage.getTileConfig() reads title/icon/iconType/backgroundColor/textColor/linkType/linkValue straight off the def and never looks at content; (3) showTitle:false is set on the four KPI stat widgets that render inside CnWidgetWrapper, so they stay header-less exactly as they were under the bare CnWidgetGrid — without it a non-card widget would grow a header captioned with its own widget id; recent-activity-feed and pending-apps-queue are the deliberate exceptions, carrying def-level titles so the wrapper renders their headers (wrapper caption = customTitle || def.title || widgetId). Tiles bypass the wrapper entirely, so they carry no showTitle. CONDITIONAL WIDGETS: pending-apps-queue is the only survivor of the original three conditional banners — the two migration banners stayed out for good (MigrationResumeBanner in App.vue shows migration state app-wide, and the error state is unreachable server-side) and the pending-apps banner grew into the real approval queue. It relies on two post-2.8.2 library behaviours (restyle follow-ups 4b + 4c): a def-level visibleWhen collapses the widget's whole grid cell while unmet (with the grid's first paint held until predicates settle, so nothing pops in and reflows the page), and endpointSource tables forward a client-side `limit` so the View-all footer can render. This entry therefore REQUIRES @conduction/nextcloud-vue > 2.8.2.

widgets.title: Applications awaiting approval
widgets._note: The admin approval queue itself, replacing the earlier keepiq-pending-apps banner (which could only say THAT applications were waiting, not WHICH — the library gained the two pieces this needs: a def-level visibleWhen collapses any widget's grid cell while unmet, and endpointSource tables forward a client-side `limit` so the View-all footer condition can hold). visibleWhen gates on the summary's pending_apps_count: non-admins get null and admins with an empty queue get 0, so the whole card — row included — exists only for an admin with pending work. Rows come from GET /api/v1/applications/pending (a bare array: id, name, registeredBy — null means an anonymous registration, createdAt ISO-8601 rendered relative via format:date-time). VIEW-ALL FOOTER: the object-table host adapter (objectTableContentToProps in CnWidgetObjectTable/dashboardRegistration.js) forwards `limit` as a prop of its own for an endpointSource table since the library fix that followed 2.36.3, checked on the installed 2.57.1, so the footer appears from a fourth pending application. On 2.36.3 and earlier `limit` was dropped and every row rendered. rowRoute carries the navigation meanwhile and regardless: any row opens the applications page, router-pushed (a route NAME, never a full page load — the vault master key is memory-only, so a reload would re-lock it and land on /lock). Deliberately NOT ApplicationDetail (/applications/:id, which does exist): the queue's job is to get an admin to the page that handles the whole queue, not to one application. The cost of that choice is one dev-only console line per click — the widget's rowRoute always pushes `params: {id}` and vue-router discards the param this path has no segment for.

ADR-049 dissolution of the keepiq-kpi-card custom widget — endpoint-bound KPI tiles against GET /api/dashboard/summary. Bound to the payload keys DashboardService::fetchSummary actually emits (total_secrets / shared_with_me_count / folders_count); the legacy view read shared_secrets / folder_count / compromised_count, which the backend never sends. The 'Possibly compromised' card is dropped: compromised_count does not exist in the summary payload, so it was a permanently-zero dead binding. COLOR IDENTITY: each KPI keeps one constant color via valueColor — total-secrets primary, folders success, rotation-due error, shared-with-me deliberately unset (theme default). TOKEN CHOICE: the *-text variants (--color-success-text / --color-error-text), NOT the bare --color-success / --color-error — on current Nextcloud server builds the bare tokens are pale BACKGROUND tints (verified live: #D8F3DA / #FFE7E7), while the *-text variants are the readable strong colors on both old and new server generations. CnStatWidget's icon circle falls back to valueColor when iconColor is unset, so valueColor alone colors both the number and the icon. A variantWhen threshold rule on rotation-due was considered and skipped: first-match variantWhen overrides the static color, which would break the constant identity this change restores.

Rotation-due count (rotation-expiry-policies §7.2) — open rotation flags for the caller's secrets, from DashboardService::fetchSummary rotation_due_count. Deep-dive detail lives in the password-health report's rotation category.

widgets.title: Recent activity
widgets._note: Ported from the pre-rename WIP: replaces the recent-activity-text ADR-049 placeholder with a live feed off GET /api/v1/audit/me — a plain app endpoint, so the object-table widget's endpointSource, not the OpenRegister-bound object-list. Verified against the backend: AuditController::mine returns {entries:[...]} newest-first (AuditEntryMapper orders occurred_at DESC) and AuditEntry::jsonSerialize emits occurredAt as ISO-8601 ('c'), eventType and objectName. The occurredAt column carries format:'date-time' so CnCellRenderer renders it through NcDateTime (relative time), not raw ISO. No rowRoute: audit entries have no detail page. viewAllRoute NOW WORKS — the original attempt had to omit it as dead config (endpointSource mode forwarded no client limit, restyle follow-up 4b, fixed in the same library release as the cell collapse): the endpoint is asked for 6 entries while the client shows 5, so the View-all footer appears exactly when a sixth entry exists, linking to the My activity page. Def-level title and no showTitle:false, so CnWidgetWrapper renders the 'Recent activity' header.

widgets.title: Recently used
widgets._note: vault-21: the secrets the user read last, one row per secret, newest first, at most five, only secrets the user still owns (GET /api/v1/secrets/recent, a bare array of id, name, typeId, lastUsedAt; RecentlyUsedService). rowRoute pushes {name: SecretList, params: {id}}, which is /secrets/:id and opens the detail sidebar, router-pushed so the memory-only vault key survives.

content.emptyText: You have not opened any secrets yet

widgets._note: Union of the bump-ncvue branch's real quick-action tiles with development's ADR-049 placeholder text; wired here in place of the quick-actions-text placeholder since these already point at live deep links. Tile fields sit at the def's top level because CnDashboardPage.getTileConfig() reads them from there, not from content. LINK SHAPE: both in-app tiles use linkType 'route', which the tile widgets push through the host vue-router. linkType 'app' resolved to a FULL page load, and the vault master key is memory-only, so every tile click re-locked the vault and landed on /lock — and the old 'keepiq#/secrets' values were dead weight on top, because main.js routes with createWebHistory and the hash fragment is never read (an earlier revision of this note claimed createWebHashHistory; that stale claim made the hash links look correct on review). The values carry ?action=create / ?action=register, which SecretList and ApplicationRegisterView consume (open the create/register dialog) and then strip from the URL. Requires @conduction/nextcloud-vue with route-type tile support (CnTileWidget/CnDashTileWidget router navigation).
widgets.title: New secret
widgets._iconNote: mdi key-plus, verbatim (vue-material-design-icons/KeyPlus.vue) — the plus badge sits UNDER the key; that is the published glyph, kept unmodified on purpose. A hand-recomposed side-badge variant was tried and dropped: stock MDI beats a custom remix.

pages.title: Reports

config.description: Pick a report to open it.

cards.label: Password health
cards.description: Weak, reused and ageing passwords in your unlocked vault.

cards.label: My activity
cards.description: Everything you did, from the audit trail.

pages._note: ADR-112 / ADR-114 Decision 3: Keepiq already had two reports, and they were two footer menu entries. Nothing is invented here — the pages stay exactly as they were, routable by the same names, and their menu entries are deleted so a report is a card OR an entry, never both (ADR-112 Decision 2). Deleted rather than listed in menu-layout's `removals`: that key retires an entry that still EXISTS, and gate-53 reports a removal naming an absent entry as a stale removal. Password health is a MEMORY-ONLY analysis over the unlocked vault, which is why it is type:"custom" rather than an object-backed page, and why it reports nothing while the vault is locked.

pages.title: My activity
pages._note: The session user's own audit-trail entries (add-secret-audit-trail §5.3). type:"custom" — a simple actor-scoped feed view, no built-in page type models it.

pages.title: Approve a share
pages._note: The owner's answer to a share request or a new group member (#747). The Approve action on those notifications opens it, with the ids in the query. type:"custom" because approving encrypts the owner's copy in the tab, which no built-in page type does. No menu entry: it is reached from a notification only.

pages.title: Password health
pages._note: Client-side vault health report (password-health). type:"custom" — the analysis runs in-browser over the unlocked vault; no built-in page type models a memory-only analysis surface.

pages.title: Certificates
pages._note: Certificate inventory (certificate-lifecycle). type:"custom" — stored certificate secrets are decrypted and X.509-parsed in-browser (ADR-003); only non-secret display metadata is submitted. Suite/CA rows are server-parsed from cleartext PEM.

pages.title: Emergency access
pages._note: Break-glass emergency access (add-emergency-access). type:"custom" — the grantor designates contacts and builds recovery envelopes in-browser; a grantee requests and recovers a grantor's key client-side. No built-in page type models this zero-knowledge escrow surface.

pages.title: Unlock Keepiq
pages._note: Master-password setup + unlock flow. Cannot use a built-in page type because the lock screen owns its own full-page layout (no app nav / header / sidebar) and gates router navigation via App.vue's lock-redirect watcher. Stays type:"custom" until the lib gains a dedicated unlock-page primitive.

pages.title: Vault
pages._note: Main vault: searchable/sortable/paginated secret list on the app nav's folder tree. type:"custom" because it owns bespoke list rows and on-demand client-side decryption that no built-in page type models yet. The optional :id? segment opens the secret-detail sidebar OVER the list — /secrets/<id> deep links keep working, and keeping the page id stable means CnPageRenderer never remounts the list when a row opens (its render key is the page id).

pages.title: Vault
pages._note: Same vault view filtered to a folder (folderId route param); :id? opens the secret-detail sidebar with the folder context kept in the path.

pages.title: Archive
pages._note: The vault list in its archived state (vault-trash-and-archive): SecretList reads the route name and asks for state=archived. :id? opens the detail sidebar over the Archive view.

pages.title: Trash
pages._note: The vault list in its trashed state (vault-trash-and-archive): restore or delete for good through the selection strip. No detail sidebar: a trashed secret is restored before it is opened.

pages.title: Incoming from other organisations
pages._note: Secrets that users of partner instances shared with this user (sharing-federated-recipients task 3.2). type:"custom" because accepting asks the server to pull ciphertext from the partner over OCM, which no built-in page type does.

pages.title: Applications
pages._note: Developer-facing app registration page. Owner sees their own apps + can register new ones; the admin approval queue is ApplicationQueueSection in the Keepiq admin settings.

pages.title: Application
pages._note: Per-application detail page. Shows metadata, EncryptionSuite info, application-attributed secrets list, and the write-secret-for-app dialog. Owner sees own + active; admin sees all (server enforces).

pages.title: Fill in secret
pages._note: Public fill-in page (no auth). The lock-screen redirect guard in App.vue exempts this route by name — see PUBLIC_ROUTE_NAMES — so an external recipient can complete the flow without a Nextcloud account; the controller runs as #[PublicPage].

pages.title: Secure message
pages._note: Public ephemeral-send access page (no auth; ephemeral-send §5.3). Exempt from the lock guard via PUBLIC_ROUTE_NAMES; the EphemeralSendAccessController endpoints run as #[PublicPage]. Fragment-mode content keys ride the URL fragment (#k=) and never reach the server.

pages.title: Shared secret
pages._note: Public link-share access page (no auth). The lock-screen redirect guard in App.vue exempts this route by name — see PUBLIC_ROUTE_NAMES — so an external recipient can complete the password-protected flow without a Nextcloud account; the LinkShareAccessController endpoints run as #[PublicPage]. Implements the two-phase recipient protocol: Phase 1 fetches the ciphertext + Argon2id salt; Phase 2 confirms a successful client-side decrypt so the server can increment the usage count and auto-delete on cap.

pages.title: Flows
pages._note: ADR-110 Decision 4: a flow is app-specific, so the authoring surface lives here rather than behind a deep link to another app's list. An ordinary index over the named `flows` source (config.entitySource) rather than the deprecated `flows` page type, reading OpenRegister's one native flow store (ADR-065), scoped to this app by config.app.

pages.title: Flow
pages._note: The shared CnFlowDetail canvas over the same single engine. Controls render in the NC app sidebar (sidebarComponent) so the canvas keeps full width; canvas and sidebar share useFlowStore. The _note claimed this before the field existed, so #/flows/new -- and every #/flows/:id -- rendered a bare canvas with no way to name, describe, trigger or step-edit the flow. Mirrors pipelinq#1490.
